text:
emma: Heads-up — customer reported intermittent 503s, says there's no trace id in the payload they captured. What’s the shortest, lowest-friction set of asks we can send them to get a repro and a trace?

 diego: Quick checklist I use: minimal curl, HAR (if browser), SDK log snippet (if mobile/web SDK), and a short note of the timestamp + region. Also request the API key prefix (masked) so we can find it in logs.

 emma: Can you drop example curl + exact header names? Customer gets nervous if we ask for raw tokens.

 ryan: Yep — ask them to redact the token but include the Authorization header name and the API key prefix (first 6 chars). Key headers we care about: `x-rw-request-ref` (our request ref), `x-edge-correlation-id` (edge id), `x-rw-session-ref` (session), and standard `x-request-id`. If none are present, ask for the raw response headers they saw.

 ryan: Minimal curl I send:

 ```
 curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
   -H "X-RW-Client: acmeapp-v1" \
   -d '{"input":"test"}' \
   "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate?model=foo"
 ```

 ryan: Ask them to paste the full response headers (not body) and mark any `x-rw-*` or `x-edge-*` headers. If they can include `x-rw-request-ref` value that's ideal.

 emma: For browser folks, what’s the HAR ask?

 diego: Steps for HAR (short): open DevTools -> Network -> reproduce -> right-click -> Save as HAR with content. Ask them to filter for the request to `api.redwood` and include that single entry. Tell them to redact Authorization.

 diego: If they can’t export HAR, ask for: request/response headers + response status + timing info from the network tab (startTime, duration).

 emma: Mobile SDKs?

 ryan: Android: ask for `logcat` lines around the call, grep for `RequestRef` or `x-rw-request-ref`. Example grep: `adb logcat -d | grep -E "(RequestRef|x-rw-request-ref|rw_reqref)"`

 ryan: iOS: ask for console logs (Xcode device logs) and the SDK debug output. Provide the exact snippet we instruct to print: `logger.info("rw_reqref=%s", response.requestRef)` — one-liners are easier for customers to run.

 emma: If they can’t get SDK logs, any fallback?

 diego: Server/proxy logs work: for nginx/envoy, grep access logs for `x-rw-request-ref` or the API key prefix. One-liner: `grep "abcd12" /var/log/nginx/* | tail -n 200` (where `abcd12` is key prefix). Also check upstream 5xx timestamps.

 emma: How do we create a debug token or attach a debug bundle?

 ryan: We have a Console flow: Console -> Support -> Create debug snapshot. But for quick triage you can ask the customer to include their request-ref and we generate the debug bundle on our side. If they want to share a debug token they can click "Generate Debug Token" in their project settings and share the token string (it’s short-lived).

 emma: Can we show an example request we’ll make internally? I’ll paste this to customer so they know what we’ll look for.

 ryan: Internally we do: find request by header or key prefix, then follow trace through edge logs and runtime. Example query: `search logs where header.x-rw-request-ref = "<reqref>"` and `search edge where x-edge-correlation-id = "<edgeid>"`

 emma: Good. I’ll send a consolidated template to the customer. Draft below — please call out anything dangerous or confusing: 

 ```
 Hi — to help us debug the intermittent 503s please provide: 
 1) A minimal curl reproducer (redact tokens but include API key prefix). Example:
    curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"input":"test"}' "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate?model=foo"

 2) Response headers (copy/paste the full headers from the client or network tab).

 3) If browser: the single HAR entry for the failing request (export & attach).

 4) If mobile: a short SDK log snippet around the failure (search for `RequestRef` / `reqref`).

 5) Approx timestamp (UTC) and region they called from, plus the API key prefix (first 6 chars).

 We will: lookup the request in edge/runtime logs, generate a debug bundle, and follow up within 24h.
 ```

 diego: +1. Add: "If you see `502`/`503` without any `x-rw-request-ref`, include the raw response body and headers" — sometimes proxies strip headers.

 infra-bot: Checklist created: [minimal-curl, har, sdk-logs, timestamp, key-prefix] :white_check_mark:

 ryan: One more pro tip — sometimes load-balancer/front door injects `x-request-id` but strips vendor headers. Ask them to check any edge/proxy config (Cloudflare/AKAMAI) if headers are missing.

 emma: Perfect. I’ll send to customer now. Tagging @ryan for any runtime follow-up if we find edge-correlation. :wave:
